source_span: There is only a 68% market probability the FOMC hikes at the upcoming meeting, even though Warsh's speech says he tightens
source_chain: Warsh's Jackson Hole speech was rhetorically hawkish, and Governor Barr echoed a hawkish tone, therefore one would expect near-certain hike pricing this close to the meeting (historically 90-100% at 15 days out) — therefore the fact that pricing sits at only 68% (an unusually LOW reading for this point in the cycle) shows the market is NOT convinced by the hawkish rhetoric — therefore softening data (ISM, JOLTS) plus the Dallas Fed trimmed-mean measure already near target (2.35%) give Warsh room to find 'wiggle room' and hold rather than hike — therefore Blitz's own call is that Warsh finds that room and holds. Invalidation: the August CPI print on 9/11 is 'the final word' for the meeting — a hot print removes the wiggle room.
pulse_chain: Fed-hike odds surged 27% to 69%, therefore the bond market has 'decided' the Fed hikes and long bonds are breaking in three countries at once — therefore vol-control/risk-parity funds, maxed at the 100th percentile, face $163bn of mechanical selling in a down market — therefore this pricing is conviction-driven (Warsh's hawkish message plus Barr) rather than data-driven, even though the data is softening — therefore the hold case is being made by Goldman, citing a soft core-CPI expectation and the Dallas Fed trimmed mean at 2.35%, despite Goldman's own screen showing 66% hike odds — therefore the September 11 CPI print (per JPMorgan) and Friday's payrolls resolve it, with a second negative payroll print taking the hike off the table.
why: The pulse inverts TS Lombard/Blitz's actual point (that 68% hike pricing is unusually LOW for this point in the cycle, meaning the market doubts Warsh's hawkish tone and Blitz expects a hold) into 'Warsh's hawkish message has convinced the market,' and it reassigns Blitz's hold-case evidence (Dallas Fed trimmed mean 2.35%, softening data) to Goldman, a bank whose only appearance in the sourced documents is a market-wrap 66% probability quote with no hold argument attached.
